title: Preparation, Administration, and Assessment of In Vivo Tissue-Specific Cellular Uptake of Fluorescent Dye-Labeled Liposomes
protocol: Combine DSPC, cholesterol, and PEG-2000-DSPE at a mass ratio of 2:1:1.
Add DiD lipid dye at a concentration of 1 mg per 1 ml of liposomes (molar ratio of 46:1 of DSPC:DiD).
Mix the lipid mixture with an ether-chloroform solution in a 20 mL scintillation vial.
Prepare an inverted phase emulsion by mixing the organic phase (lipid mixture) and aqueous phase (calcium acetate, 1 M, pH 7.4) at a ratio of 4:1.
Emulsify the ether-chloroform solution of lipids by sonication for 30 s at room temperature.
Operate the sonicator at 20 KHz and 50% power using a ½ in. probe.
Keep the tip of the sonicator probe closer to the bottom of the vial to avoid foaming.
Immediately place the vial with homogenized water-in-oil emulsion on a rotary evaporator with a special adapter, manometer gauge, and pressure regulator valve.
Set the rotation rate at 100 rpm and the vacuum at 0.5 atm.
Release the vacuum if emulsion foaming looks excessive.
Increase the vacuum to 0.9 atm after a gel forms and disappears.
Adjust vacuum level gradually during volatile organic phase removal to avoid rapid foaming.
Continue evaporation until gel disappears and remaining aqueous media is completely liquid again.
Place a polytetrafluoroethylene stir bar into the evaporation flask to enhance convection of the viscous gel.
Filter resultant liposomes using track-etched polycarbonate membranes to achieve homogeneous size distribution.
Perform filtration by passing the liposome aqueous dispersion back-and-forth multiple times through a 200 nm-pore polycarbonate filter in a liposome extruder equipped with two gas-tight syringes.
Mix an odd number of filtrations (e.g., 21) to ensure the resulting material ends up on the opposite side from the start.
Add 1 to 3 mL of saline to a 1 cm cuvette with four transparent sides.
Add 10‒20 µL of liposomes and mix carefully.
Place the sample into the dynamic laser light scattering apparatus.
Select solvent viscosity, refractive index, and refractive index of lipids parameters for measurement.
Click the Start button to begin measurements.
Remove external Ca-acetate using a desalting spin-column.

Pre-equilibrate the 2-mL desalting spin-column with 10 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.4) prior to use by spinning in a centrifuge at 1000 x g for 2 min, removing the pass-through buffer and repeating this four times.
Add aqueous tesaglitazar in 10 mM HEPES buffer (pH 7.4) to half of the batch.
Incubate with mixing at 37 °C for 1 h.
Use the second half of the batch as a drug-free control liposome formulation.
Pre-equilibrate the 2-mL desalting spin-column again if not already done so and add no more than 0.5 mL of liposome sample to the dry column gel bed.
Wait until all the sample enters the gel before centrifuging at exactly the same conditions (1000 x g, 2 min).
Collect the liposome sample in the pass-through purified from small molecular mass compounds.
Quantify final particle features: particle size and concentration using DLS and zeta potential with a combined DLS-electrophoretic light scattering (ELS) system in 10 mM HEPES buffer pH 7.4 at 25 °C.
Dilute liposome dispersion in the measurement buffer (e.g., 1 mL of buffer solution containing 10 µL liposomes) into a U-shaped cuvette using a disposable Luer syringe or pipette with a cut tip.
Ensure there are no bubbles in the “U” to allow uninterrupted solution for electrical current flow.
Place the cuvette into the unit ensuring electrodes are properly connected.
Close the instrument door and start the measurement under guidance software control.
In a biosafety cabinet, dilute liposomes in sterile saline to an appropriate concentration for in vivo administration, reaching a final volume of 50 µL.
Quantify the number of liposomes per unit volume using DLS/ELS to ensure equal numbers are administered compared to drug-loaded preparations.
Load the diluted liposome solution into a 27 G needle while maintaining room temperature.
Administer the liposome solution via retro-orbital intravenous injection.
Clean the workbench with 70% ethanol.
Select a space that permits the use of an isoflurane anesthesia system.
Turn on a warming pad and place a clean pad or towel over it.
Allow enough time for the pad to warm up before beginning work with mice.
Set up the anesthesia system so that the chamber is nearby and the nose cone is on the warming pad.
Ensure all aspects of the system are ready, such as sufficient isoflurane level in the vaporizer and correctly connected tubing.
Gather ophthalmic lubricant gel, a local anesthetic for post-administration treatment, and sterile gauze pads.
Sedate the mouse using isoflurane in the induction chamber.
Transfer the mouse to the workspace while maintaining sedation through a nose cone once unresponsive to a gentle foot tap.
Maintain the animal at 1.5% to 2.5% isoflurane and assess for an appropriate depth of anesthesia via lack of response to toe pinch.
Shift the mouse to one side for liposome administration.
Apply a small amount of ophthalmic lubricant to both eyes to keep them moisturized during the remainder of the procedure.
Gently press down on the skin above and below the exposed eye.
Insert the tip of the needle at the medial canthus, ensuring it is below the eye and not touching it.
Slowly inject the liposomes into the retro-orbital space once the needle is inserted correctly.
Close the eyelids for a few seconds upon withdrawing the needle to achieve hemostasis.
Apply proparacaine or another local anesthetic to the eye post-procedure.
Keep the mouse on a warming pad and monitor until it awakens to ensure proper body temperature maintenance.
Return the mouse to its cage after monitoring.

Prepare solutions for tissue harvest, processing, and flow cytometry staining (phosphate-buffered saline-Heparin, HEPES Buffer, 2 mg/mL Collagenase type I, AKC lysis buffer, FACS buffer, PBS, Fixation buffer).
Maintain all solutions at 4 °C or on ice during the procedure except for the fixation buffer.
Prepare tubes with buffers and other materials for harvesting and processing tissues.
Clean the bench space with 70% ethanol.
Prepare a rubber tray for pinning the mouse during harvest by cleaning it off with 70% ethanol and covering it with an absorbent pad or paper towels.
Fill a 10 mL syringe with PBS-heparin and fasten on a 25 G needle for perfusion.

Gather tools and materials to use during the harvest, including two pairs of forceps, scissors, paper towels, lint-free wipes, microcentrifuge tubes with EDTA, microcentrifuge tubes with HEPES buffer, and polyethylene vials with HEPES buffer.
Euthanize the mouse by CO2 asphyxiation.
Set up a rubber dissection tray and a bucket of ice for samples.
Spray down the mouse with 70% ethanol.
Place the mouse on its back on the rubber tray.
Pin down the mouse’s paws spread out away from its body.
Make an incision in the skin at the edge of the caudal end of the ribcage.
Cut a small, straight line up towards the mouse’s head until the pectoralis muscles are exposed.
Make two small cuts perpendicular to the initial line.
Carefully cut away the pectoralis muscle on one side of the rib cage.
Insert the needle between the third and fourth ribs where the muscle was removed.
Keep the needle close to the center line of the rib cage.
Gently pull up on the syringe to begin collecting blood.
Transfer collected blood to a prepared microcentrifuge tube with EDTA.
Store the tube on ice.
Rotate the syringe if no blood enters after pulling up about 100 µL volume.
Move the needle further into the chest cavity if rotation does not help.
Continue to pull back slowly if blood begins to collect in the syringe.
Remove the needle and try reinserting if no blood is collected.
Cut the skin along the end of the rib cage down to the mouse’s side on each side for perfusion.
Use forceps to hold up the sternum away from the working surface.
Make a small, shallow incision just below the end of the sternum to cut through the peritoneal cavity.
Cut along the peritoneal membrane along the end of the rib cage on each of the mouse’s sides.
Avoid cutting into the liver and gallbladder during the cuts.
Make a small, shallow cut into the diaphragm cranial to the liver.
Cut the diaphragm along the edge of the rib cage to open up the chest cavity.
Be sure to avoid cutting any organs within the chest cavity.
Make two cuts along the rib cage towards the head about 2-3 mm from the center line and about 0.75 cm long.
Lift back the center piece of the rib cage to expose the chest cavity.
Move fat or tissue away to access the heart.
Make a small cut into the right atrium of the mouse’s heart to create an opening.
Insert the needle of a 10 mL syringe filled with PBS-heparin into the left ventricle of the mouse’s heart.
Gently begin pushing PBS into the heart as slowly as possible.
Observe blood emerging from the right atria and filling the chest cavity.
Discard the syringe and needle once all 10 mL of PBS-heparin have been perfused through the mouse.
Remove excess blood and PBS-heparin from the chest cavity using paper towels or lint-free wipes.
Cut down the skin and peritoneal membrane towards the mouse’s tail to open up the peritoneal cavity.
Extract the inguinal adipose tissue pad from each side of the mouse.
Extract the inguinal lymph node from each depot carefully.
Hold the peritoneal membrane and skin edge with forceps.
Gently pull the skin away from the peritoneal membrane to separate them.
Locate the inguinal adipose tissue depot along the skin.
Pin down the outer edge of the skin for better access.
Identify the three larger arteries running towards the center of the depot.
Remove the lymph node where these arteries meet using forceps and scissors as needed.
Hold the end of the adipose depot nearest to the pinned point with forceps.
Make small cuts at the connective membrane between the adipose tissue and skin.
Lift the adipose tissue away from the skin while making cuts to ensure complete extraction.
Place the extracted adipose depot in a prepared polyethylene vial containing HEPES buffer on ice.
Extract both epididymal adipose depots from the caudal end of the peritoneal cavity.
Gently pull the first epididymal adipose depot away from the dorsal end of the mouse.
Locate the epididymis and vas deferens attached to this depot.
Carefully cut between the adipose depot and the epididymis and vas deferens to separate the adipose tissue.
Place the separated adipose depot in a polyethylene vial with HEPES buffer on ice.
Extract the spleen from the left side of the stomach near the diaphragm.
Gently pull the stomach towards the center of the peritoneal cavity to expose the spleen.
Hold one end of the spleen and gently pull it away from the stomach.
Cut the membrane between the spleen and its adjacent tissue until the organ is detached.
Place the spleen in a prepared microcentrifuge tube with HEPES buffer and store on ice.
Mince the adipose tissue in each polyethylene vial until it is in small pieces less than 0.5 mm in size using one or two pairs of scissors.
Add 1.5 mL of 2 mg/mL Collagenase buffer to each vial containing minced adipose tissue.
Place the vials in a shaking incubator set to 37 °C and 150 rpm.
Incubate for 30 to 45 min.
If necessary, add another 0.5 mL to 1.5 mL of HEPES buffer and an equal volume of Collagenase buffer to ensure tissues are fully submerged and enough enzyme is present.
Gently shake the samples every 5 min if using a water bath heated to 37 °C instead of a shaking incubator.
Check the samples at 30 min.
Use a 1 mL pipette to pipet the sample up and down.
If tissue pieces are too large, return the samples to the incubator for an additional 15 min.
Pipet the cell suspension through a 70 μm filter into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 5 mL of FACS buffer to the empty digestion vial to wash it out.
Transfer this wash buffer through the filter to add to the cell suspension.
Store samples on ice while others are being processed.
Spin samples at 400 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the adipocyte supernatant by aspiration.
Carefully remove the infranatant between the adipocyte supernatant and pellet by aspiration.
Resuspend the stromal-vascular fraction (SVF) pellet in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Transfer the SVF to a clean 1.5 or 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Aliquot cells if desired or needed.
Keep on ice until all samples are ready for flow cytometry staining.
Transfer 50 μL of blood to a 15-mL conical tube.
Add 1 mL of AKC lysis buffer to each tube and pipette up and down to reach a single-cell suspension.
Add an additional 4 mL of AKC lysis buffer to each tube and incubate for 5‒10 min.
Seal the tube caps tightly and place the tubes on a shaker or rotator if available, to enhance mixing.
Add 5 mL of FACS buffer to quench the lysis process.
Spin the samples at 400 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and check the pellet.
If the pellet is still quite red, repeat the lysis process.
Otherwise, resuspend the pellets in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Transfer to a clean 1.5 or 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Keep on ice until all samples are ready for flow cytometry staining.
Transfer the spleen onto a 70 µm filter over a 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the tissue with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Mash the spleen through the filter using the plunger end of a 1 mL syringe.
Continue washing the cells into the conical tube with more FACS buffer.
Ensure the final volume in the conical tube is 10 mL.
Spin the cells at 300 x g at 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend in 1 mL of AKC lysis buffer.
Add an additional 4 mL of AKC lysis buffer and incubate for 5 min.
Add 5 mL of FACS buffer to quench the lysis process.
Spin the samples at 300 x g at 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Transfer the suspension through a second, clean 70 µm filter into a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 4 mL of FACS buffer to wash out the original tube.
Transfer the buffer through the filter for a final volume of 5 mL.
Transfer 50 μL of the cell suspension to a clean 1.5 or 1.7 mL microcentrifuge tube and keep on ice until all samples are ready for flow cytometry staining.
Spin down aliquoted samples at 400 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove supernatant from samples.
Resuspend samples in 50 μL of Fc Block (diluted).
Incubate on ice for 5 min.
Add 50 μL of 2x antibody mix to each sample.
Incubate on ice in the dark for 20 min.
Wash samples with 1 mL of PBS.
Spin at 400 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend samples in viability stain (Table 3).
Incubate on ice in the dark for 20 min.
Stain cells that were set aside for a Live/Dead single stain during this step.
Wash samples with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Spin at 400 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend samples in 50 μL of fixation medium (Reagent A).
Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 15 min.
Resuspend Live/Dead single stain in 100 μL of 2% PFA.
Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 5 min.
Wash sample with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Spin at 800 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove supernatant and resuspend samples in 250 to 500 μL of FACS buffer.
Store at 4 °C until analysis on the flow cytometer.
Wash samples with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Spin samples at 800 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend samples in 50 μL of permeabilization medium plus antibody/ies to intracellular proteins.
Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 20 min.
Wash the samples with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Spin samples at 800 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend samples in 100 μL of 2% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 5 min.
Wash samples with 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Spin samples at 800 x g, 4 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend samples in 250 to 500 μL of FACS buffer.
Store samples at 4 °C until analysis on the flow cytometer.
